open_points.subject: sandbox environment and filesystem access
open_points.text: The formal environment now includes `own_proc`, but rule 1 still says, “No host directory is mounted except the read-only runtime and that exchange directory,” and rule 4 raises on “opening any path outside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime.” Nothing defines `own_proc`, its mount, contents, permissions, or whether the audit hook permits access to it.
open_points.question: What exactly is `own_proc`, and may function code open paths in it despite the rule-4 path trap?
options: `own_proc` is an accessible private `/proc` mount and is an exception to the path trap
`own_proc` exists only for sandbox/process plumbing and function code cannot open it
The formal addition is erroneous and no proc filesystem is present
open_points.default_guess: Treat `own_proc` as sandbox plumbing inaccessible to function code, so opens there remain sandbox violations.

witness.initial: An admitted function has a value output and otherwise conforming code.
events: The function opens `/proc/self/stat` and returns data derived from it.
The sandbox runner applies the new `environment = {..., own_proc}` rule and the unchanged audit-hook rule.
outcomes: The private proc entry is readable because `own_proc` is part of the execution environment, and the function can succeed.
Opening it is outside the exchange directory and runtime, so the trap is recorded and the execution concludes `sandbox_violation`.
witness.observer: The caller sees either a successful run output or a sandbox failure.

open_points.subject: K-02 function purity and State 0 product boundary
open_points.text: State 0 defines nodes as “a pure function” and excludes clock and randomness, while changed K-02 says code that gets time or chance by another way “is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other”; changed A03 test 6 guarantees repeatability only when the implementation obtains no time and no chance.
open_points.question: Is equal input required to yield equal output for every admitted function, or may an admitted function deliberately use an untrapped time/chance source and vary between executions?
options: Purity remains an invariant, so implementations capable of varying on equal inputs must be prevented or refused
Only the listed entry points are prohibited; other time/chance use and unequal outputs are permitted
Purity means only absence of effects, not deterministic output
open_points.default_guess: Interpret purity as no external effects and permit unequal outputs obtained through untrapped sources, because the changed text explicitly limits detection and repeatability.

witness.initial: A contract has one input, one valid integer output, and a trial case whose expected output is absent. Its implementation reads an untrapped standard-library timing source such as `resource.getrusage(...).ru_utime` and returns a value derived from it.
events: An author submits the implementation when its trial execution succeeds, so A04 records an admitted verdict and activates it.
A caller runs the active flow twice with the same input.
outcomes: Under State 0's pure-function/no-clock/no-randomness promise, both executions must have the same output or the implementation must not be admitted.
Under changed K-02 and A03, the untrapped source is not detected, both schema-valid executions succeed, and the callers may receive different outputs.
witness.observer: The owner or agent reading the two run outputs sees whether equal inputs can produce unequal outputs.

open_points.subject: admission and the repaired-corpus guarantee
open_points.text: K-05 says a failed execution can be captured “so a repaired slot stays repaired,” and A04 concludes “A repaired slot stays repaired,” but changed A03 permits an implementation that obtains time or chance to give different results on later executions, while A04 records and reuses the verdict from one execution of each case.
open_points.question: Does passing each corpus case once permanently establish that the implementation stays repaired, or is the guarantee intentionally lost for implementations that obtain time or chance?
options: The repaired-slot guarantee applies to every admitted implementation and therefore requires repeatable behavior on corpus inputs
Admission is only evidence about the executions recorded at admission; the same implementation may later fail the captured input
Implementations that obtain time or chance need a separate admission or activation rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat admission as one recorded observation only and drop the claim that such an implementation stays repaired.

witness.initial: A function failed on input `x`; that failed execution was captured as a trial case with no expected output. A replacement implementation uses an untrapped timing source and fails on `x` for some readings but succeeds for others.
events: The agent submits the replacement while its one admission execution on `x` succeeds.
The kernel records `admitted`, activates it, and reuses that verdict for the same implementation and corpus.
A later real run executes the function on `x` when the timing-dependent branch fails.
outcomes: The repaired-slot passages imply the captured failure cannot recur after the replacement is admitted.
The changed A03 rule plus A04's one recorded verdict allow the later run to fail on the same captured input without any new admission refusal.
witness.observer: The run caller sees the supposedly repaired captured case fail again.
